findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the pinned pypandoc extra guarantees a pandoc binary on every supported platform/venue (bundled binary vs. system install), and define the fallback when pandoc is unavailable (e.g. degrade to identity passthrough rather than crash the DC send).
evidence: Plan: "render structurally-safe units (headings, lists, code, quotes, safe paragraphs) to wiki via pinned `pandoc`"
Plan Scope: "`pyproject.toml` — pinned `pypandoc` extra."
Fact: plain `pypandoc` shells out to a system pandoc; only the `pypandoc_binary` extra bundles a binary, and that bundle does not cover all OS/arch combinations.
findings.finding: The renderer bakes a native `pandoc` binary into the DC outbound send path via `pypandoc`, but the plan does not establish that the pinned extra bundles the pandoc binary for every supported platform/venue; plain `pypandoc` requires a system-installed pandoc, so a deployment without it fails at send time.
findings.location: Approach / Scope — "pinned `pypandoc` extra" and "render structurally-safe units … via pinned `pandoc` (`-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`)"
scenarios: Remote MCP server (Platform: Linux/BSD server, no dev toolchain) with a DC target: a description update triggers pandoc; the binary is absent, pypandoc raises OSError, and the issue update crashes instead of shipping wiki.
Windows workstation without pandoc on PATH: the same DC send fails at render time; the user sees a runtime error rather than a fallback to verbatim passthrough.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the binary-bundling `pypandoc[binary]`/`pypandoc_binary` extra and add an availability check that falls back to identity passthrough (verbatim, echo-safe) when pandoc cannot be located, with a test for the missing-binary path.

This edit target/consumer is not enumerated, nor is it explained how to_wire gets applied on the DC update path without touching the shared composition (or how Cloud is insulated if it is).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the DC description non-convergence introduced by rendering on `to_wire` while `normalize_outbound` stays identity: specify how the compare form (`normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local))`) is made equal to the landed/decoded wiki body so the differ and reconcile_check converge.
evidence: `outbound_field_diff.py:278-293` compares `fitted = map_fields_to_remote({description: local})` (= normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local)), identity for DC) against `canonical_remote['description']`; comment: 'or the differ re-emits a description update on every pass'
`reconcile_check.py:194-198` performs the same compare with the same identity ops

Plan keeps `normalize_outbound` identity ('Leave normalize_outbound/fit_outbound … unchanged') and inbound `normalize_rich_text` unchanged, but renders on `to_wire` — so the send-form (wiki) and the compare-form (raw MD) diverge
`WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` returns text unchanged (rich_text.py:96-98); inbound decode is identity on str
findings.finding: Wiring `to_wire` (a lossy MD->wiki render) into the live DC send while leaving `normalize_outbound` and the inbound `normalize_rich_text` as identity makes the DC description differ non-convergent: the differ compares fitted-local (raw Markdown) against the inbound-decoded stored body (wiki), which never match, so every rich description is re-emitted on every pass.
findings.location: Approach / AC line 2 ('The DC outbound send applies to_wire so the description reaching update_issue is rendered wiki')
scenarios: A DC ticket with a rich description (headings/lists/code) is reconciled: pass 1 pushes wiki, pass 2 sees local MD != stored wiki and re-pushes, forever
reconcile_check reports a permanent phantom description discrepancy on every rich DC ticket
findings.suggested_fix: Either route the compare through the same render (make `normalize_outbound` reflect the wiki round-trip, i.e. `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`), or land the state-based echo suppression (3388) FIRST so the differ keys on the observed-after-push baseline rather than on `normalize_outbound(local)`. Do not ship a live lossy send without one of these in place.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the dependency direction: since `3388` depends on `e59d`, either gate the live `to_wire` send behind 3388, or add an in-story convergence guarantee so this change is safe standalone.
evidence: Ticket `3388` deps: `depends_on e59d-3418-67ff-4aff` (this plan) — 3388 is downstream, not a prerequisite

Plan states this codec 'does NOT need to be a fixed point' but wires `to_wire` into the LIVE send in the SAME story
findings.finding: The plan relies on story `3388` for echo-safety, but `3388` DEPENDS ON this story (`e59d`), so the safety mechanism lands after this change. The plan does not address the interim window (or the dependency-order inversion) in which the live DC send is lossy with no suppression.
findings.location: Context/Problem ('echo-safety comes from the separate state-suppression story 3388-…, so this codec does NOT need to be a fixed point')
scenarios: Between e59d landing and 3388 landing, every DC rich-description reconcile pass re-emits (see the convergence finding)
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `to_wire` unit-tested but NOT yet applied on the live send in this story (leave the send identity), and move the 'wire to_wire into the live send' AC into 3388 where the baseline-suppression makes it safe; or invert the dep and make 3388 a prerequisite.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Address the codec-law breakage (`normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`) that rendering on `to_wire` alone introduces, or state explicitly how the pinned law and its comment-differ consumer are kept satisfied.
evidence: `test_rich_text_codec.py:161-174` pins `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` for every codec, over realistic bodies including code fences and lists

`outbound_comments.py:44-56`: 'safe ONLY because normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) … If that law ever stops holding … a body pulled FROM Jira starts being re-emitted … silently overwriting the human's Jira-native formatting'
Under the plan: normalize_outbound('# H')='# H' but decode_inbound(to_wire('# H'))='h1. H' — law broken
findings.finding: Rendering on `to_wire` while `normalize_outbound` stays identity violates the pinned codec law `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`, which the outbound comment differ's dedup key depends on.
findings.location: Approach ('Leave normalize_outbound/fit_outbound … unchanged')
scenarios: A DC comment body that round-trips through Jira gets re-emitted or a human's wiki edit gets clobbered on the next outbound comment pass
findings.suggested_fix: Make `normalize_outbound` return `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` (the round-trip preview) so the law holds and both the description and comment differs converge — this also fixes the description non-convergence finding.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion asserting a rich DC description converges (pass-2 emits zero description updates) after `to_wire` rendering, and keep the existing DC convergence test green.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the pandoc-binary capability assertion: state explicitly whether the extra pins `pypandoc_binary` (bundled binary), pins a pandoc version as a documented system prerequisite, or provisions it another way — and note the version/feature floor at which the `-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none` invocation is supported.
evidence: Plan Scope: 'pyproject.toml — pinned `pypandoc` extra.'
Plan Approach: 'render structurally-safe units ... to wiki via pinned `pandoc`'

pyproject.toml: the `jira-datacenter` extra is `jira = ["jira>=3.8,<4"]` only; comment (lines 68-71) states 'System prerequisites (not pip deps): git, and `acli`' — i.e. this repo's precedent treats external binaries as operator-installed, not shipped by an extra
docs/user-guide.md:342-344 installs DC via `pip install 'nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]'` with no binary-provisioning step — a pandoc binary would need its own documented provisioning

ABSENCE: the plan never states whether pandoc ships as `pypandoc_binary`, is bundled by the extra, or is an operator-installed system prerequisite — the `pypandoc` pure package cannot run without a pandoc binary present
findings.finding: The renderer's entire approach depends on invoking a native pandoc binary at DC send time, but the plan does not resolve how that binary is delivered: it names only a 'pinned `pypandoc` extra', and plain `pypandoc` does not bundle the pandoc binary (that is `pypandoc_binary`, or pandoc is a separate system prerequisite). The epic's own precedent — the `jira-datacenter` extra ships only the `jira` pip package, and other external binaries (git, acli) are documented system prerequisites — makes this genuinely ambiguous rather than obvious.
findings.location: Approach + Scope ('pinned `pypandoc` extra'; 'pinned `pandoc` (`-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`)')
scenarios: An operator runs `pip install 'nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]'` on a host with no system pandoc; the first DC description send raises at pandoc invocation because `pypandoc` cannot locate a binary
CI installs the pinned extra but the render/corpus tests silently skip or error because no pandoc binary is present in the runner
findings.suggested_fix: Name the exact delivery mechanism in Scope (e.g. pin `pypandoc-binary` in a new `[jira-datacenter-wiki]`/existing extra so the binary ships, OR document pandoc >=<version> as a system prerequisite alongside git/acli in docs/user-guide.md), and add the pandoc-version floor at which the jira writer + `--wrap=none` are guaranteed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that pypandoc folds into the EXISTING [jira-datacenter] extra (not a new extra), is lazily imported, and is added to the optionality ban-list (`_optionality.yml`) so it stays absent from a no-extras install — matching the ADR-0055 confinement pattern for the DC third-party dependency.
evidence: Plan Scope line: 'pyproject.toml — pinned `pypandoc` extra.' — no statement of which extra it lands in.

ADR 0055 Consequences: 'rebar gains its first third-party runtime dependency in the reconciler, confined to `[jira-datacenter]`, lazily imported, and CI-checked absent from a default install.' (docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md:335)

.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:89 asserts a fixed module ban-list (langchain/langgraph/anthropic/inspect_ai/opentelemetry/jira) stays absent from a no-extras install; a new runtime dep must be slotted into this same confinement pattern.

The DC renderer is deployment-gated: WikiTextCodec is only constructed for DC (backend.py:84), and DC install is already gated by [jira-datacenter] (docs/architecture.md:197) — a second parallel extra for the same deployment would be redundant config/dependency surface.
findings.finding: The plan adds a 'pinned pypandoc extra' to pyproject.toml without stating whether pypandoc folds into the EXISTING [jira-datacenter] extra or creates a new separate extra, and whether it is added to the optionality ban-list and lazily imported per the established DC-dependency convention.

scenarios: A no-extras `import rebar` install pulls in pandoc/pypandoc because it was declared as a bare/new extra outside the [jira-datacenter] confinement.

findings.suggested_fix: Declare `pypandoc` under the existing `[jira-datacenter]` optional-dependency group in pyproject.toml, import it lazily inside wiki_render.py, and add `pypandoc`/`pandoc` to the `_optionality.yml` clean-wheel ban-list assertion.
